17.2 Card Sort two classifications and exact transformations
17.3 Reflecting on Reflection exact mirror axis

Task.Prompt: Given explicitly labelled congruent triangles ABC and DEF, give a pointwise translation/rotation/optional reflection sequence preserving already matched vertices. Sort four original rigid-motion cards twice with different criteria, and construct an exact mirror line for a given corresponding pair.

Criteria.Criterion: accurate correspondence labels and first translation
rotation about matched first point fixes it and aligns second point
third point proof with optional reflection in matched line
two independently justified card-sort groupings and exact mirror construction

Practice.Prompt: How can triangle ABC be mapped pointwise to D=(5,3), E=(5,5), F=(4,3)?
Practice.Expected: Translate by (5,3), then rotate 90 CCW about D; A→D, B→E, C→F.

Practice.Prompt: Which always maps distinct A to B: half-turn at A, midpoint half-turn, reflection in AB, reflection in perpendicular bisector AB, translation AB?
Practice.Expected: Midpoint half-turn, perpendicular-bisector reflection and directed translation AB.

Practice.Prompt: How can you align two congruent triangles systematically without guessing?
Practice.Expected: Translate one vertex to mate; rotate about it to align a second; reflect across their line if third lies opposite.

Practice.Prompt: Triangle rotation symmetry exchanges any vertices; what follows?
Four equally spaced petals: symmetry angles?
Right triangle has a reflection symmetry. What follows?
Practice.Expected: It is isosceles right, two equal legs and two equal acute angles.

Practice.Prompt: A kite has symmetry line AC. Compare angles ACB and ACD.
Exact mirror line mapping A to distinct B?
Two directed 60-degree rotations differ only in centre. Must outputs match?
Practice.Expected: No; centre is essential; matching angle without matching centre insufficient.

FirstPartyCooldown: EDULYTIKS_AUTHORED_COOLDOWN: translate A(0,0) to D(5,3), rotate 90 CCW about D, prove B→E and C→F
Handoff: Teacher collects actual labelled diagrams and two card-sort explanations, marks 0/1/2 for each rubric item, dates/signs offline feedback.

Cases.CORRECT: pointwise sequence maps three requested labelled vertices
Cases.EQUIVALENT: alternate valid sequences matching same point correspondence
Cases.WRONG: aligns only first point and assumes all others match
Cases.INSUFFICIENT: visual congruence claim without precise motion specification
